name: City Council Adjourned Meeting - Policy Development Session
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
  MARCH 26, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
at 12:09 p.m. in the Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR SCHMITZ.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR SCHMITZ.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, and Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan* (arrived at 12:17 p.m.)

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Analyst Carol Corea
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATION

A.  HdL COMPANIES PRESENTATION ON PROPERTY TAX TRENDS, SALES TAX
  OUTLOOK AND BUSINESS LICENSE ADMINISTRATION

Senior Accountant Estrada introduced Kenneth Brown, Connor Duckworth and Nichole Cone of
HdL Companies, who provided an update on the current state of the City’s Sales Tax, Property
Taxes and Business Licenses:

  -  RHE Sales Tax Rate Breakdown
  -  Statewide Sales Tax Trends and Major Industry Groups
  -  Percent Change in Consumer Price Index
  -  Interest Rates and California Unemployment
  -  HdL Statewide Trend Quarterly Outlook and Annual Outlook for Sales Tax
  -  Allocation of Countywide Use Tax Pool
  -  Online sales allocations
  -  Proposition 13
  -  RHE Property Tax Dollar Breakdown
  -  Historical Assessed Value Growth and RHE Value Change Causes
  -  Single-Family Residential Sales History and Detached Single-Family Homes
  -  Five-Year Property Tax Projection
  -  Legislative update on Proposition 19
  -  Tax Revenue by Fiscal Year Payment
  -  Number of Business License Accounts and Total Tax Paid by Location
  -  Business License Revenue Contribution Percentage by Rate Type
  -  Business Count Percentage by Rate Type
  -  Monthly Trends of Business Activity
  -  Monthly Business License Tax Returns
  -  Business Tax Operations

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
 Public comment was received from Andrew Rein relating to how internet sales tax is captured by
local cities.

5.  MID-YEAR ACCOMPLISHMENTS

A.  DEPARTMENTAL MID-YEAR STAFF REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

Administrative Services Department mid-year accomplishments provided by Senior Accountant
Estrada (as per the agenda material).

Administration Department mid-year accomplishments provided by Assistant City Manager
Davis (as per the agenda material), which included a Public Outreach Overview presentation.

Community Services Department mid-year report provided by Supervisor Pinuelas (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development mid-year accomplishments provided by Director Naughton (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested staff investigate the possibility of creating a solar
battery storage and microgrid for resilience program that includes resources for residents similar
to the City’s Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) program.

Public Works Department mid-year accomplishments provided by Director Wahba (as per the
agenda material).

It was the consensus of the City Council to receive and file the mid-year reports.

MAYOR SCHMITZ called for a recess at 1:21 p.m.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reconvened the meeting at 1:26 p.m.

6.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

A.  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT:
  FINANCE UPDATE, SECURITY CAMERAS, CYBER SECURITY

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

  FINANCE UPDATE

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), providing an
update on the City’s main audit activities.

This item is informational for the Council.

  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY UPDATE

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), providing
information about expanding the use of security cameras to other City facilities and parks.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to develop
a security camera implementation plan, obtain cost estimates, and allocate funds in
future budgets.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), providing a high-
level update on the City’s cybersecurity measures.

This item is informational for the Council.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
 B.  ADMINISTRATION DEPARTMENT:
  CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER/CITY HALL RENOVATION, ELECTRONIC BICYCLES
  OUTREACH AND REGULATION, USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, GUN SAFETY,
  EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

  CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER/CITY HALL RENOVATION

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
goals towards ADA accommodations, meeting energy efficiency standards and other needed
upgrades, and providing a list of recommended renovation/remodel work to be considered and
prioritized in upcoming budget years.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA suggested the Council Chamber sounds system be considered
in this renovation discussion and suggested solar/battery options be considered for City Hall, in
place or in addition to its current diesel backup generator.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to engage
the services of an engineer and architect in FY 2024-25 to develop a scope of work
focused on the City Council Chamber upgrades.

  ELECTRONIC BICYCLES (E-BIKES) OUTREACH AND REGULATIONS

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), discussing
enforcement, engineering and education.

Discussion ensued about proposed State legislation regarding e-bikes, enforcement through the
City or Sheriff’s Department, and permitting through the School District.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to wait to see how the
State chooses to legislate on e-bikes, continue working with the Sheriff’s Department on
enforcement, and continue working with the School District on expanding the permit
process implemented at Ridgecrest Intermediate School.

  USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), discussing
the opportunity to create an AI policy for a managed and responsible approach that
acknowledges the benefits of efficiency while minimizing the risks around AI bias, privacy, and
cybersecurity.

Discussion ensued about the ethical implications associated with AI.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to return to
the City Council with an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Policy.

  GUN SAFETY

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), discussing
safe storage of firearms in homes and vehicles.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA elaborated on the importance of education for the public about
safe storage of firearms.

Discussion ensued about enforcement, the School District’s educational program, and the
possibility of a gun safety program in coordination with the Sheriff’s Department.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to take no action at this
time, and to monitor State legislation and the School District’s educational program.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
   EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT UPDATE

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the City’s hazard mitigation plan, emergency operations plan, disaster district program,
evacuation planning, community-wide drill and emergency sirens.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to move
forward with a multi-jurisdictional hazard mitigation plan, emergency operations plan,
disaster district program, evacuation planning, and a community-wide drill but not
proceed with an emergency siren program.

C.  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT:
  LANDSCAPE CONTRACT, DOG PARK FEASIBILITY, PARKS AND RECREATION FEE
  STUDY, RECREATION REGISTRATION SYSTEM, FUTURE CAPITAL PROJECTS

  LANDSCAPE CONTRACT

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to prepare
a First Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Bennett Landscape to
continue landscape maintenance services for an additional year rather than issue a
Request for Proposals for a new contract.

  DOG PARK FEASIBILITY

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing the Park and Activities Commission’s suggestion that a dog park/run may provide
an additional amenity for dog owners and walkers, reducing the concern of dogs off-leash at City
parks and trails.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to move
forward with the consideration of a dog park/run and return to the City Council with
potential locations and policy.

  PARKS AND RECREATION FEE STUDY

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to include
funding for a Parks and Recreation Fee Study in the City’s proposed FY 2024-25 budget.

  RECREATION REGISTRATION SYSTEM

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

This item is informational for the Council.

  FUTURE CAPITAL PROJECTS

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
including phase 2 of Founders Park (Purchase and Installation of Play Equipment); restroom
floor refurbishing at Highridge Park and Ernie Howlett Park; drainage improvements at Tennis
Center; Highridge Park decomposed granite pathway and drainage improvements; outdoor
benches for City Parks and Tennis operations as needed; new George F Canyon Nature Center
(bids solicited in Spring 2024 and construction estimated to start in Summer 2024); and the
following annually allocated items: annual arena replenishment – as needed; ADA projects;
Scout projects.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to include
the listed Capital Improvement Projects in the City’s proposed budget year to the extent
funding is available.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
 D.  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT:
  FALSE ALARM PERMIT PROCESS, DEVELOPMENT PROJECT UPDATES, LONG-
  RANGE PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS, CODE COMPLIANCE

  FALSE ALARM PERMIT PROCESS

Administrative Analyst Corea provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about whether to charge the customers or the alarm companies, the current
City ordinance and policy on false alarm permits and enforcement by the Sheriff’s Department.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to return to
the City Council with options to improve the current alarm permit process for further
discussion.

  DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS

Community Development Director Naughton discussed this item during the Mid-Year
Accomplishments discussion.

This item is informational for the Council.

  LONG-RANGE PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS

Community Development Director Naughton discussed this item during the Mid-Year
Accomplishments discussion.

This item is informational for the Council.

  CODE COMPLIANCE

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER requested more information be provided to the Council in
the biannual code compliance report regarding the status of code compliance cases including
long-term or recurring cases.

Director Naughton explained how staff is refining the available fields of the report in the backend
of the database of the code compliance module, to further clarify the way the information is
reported to the Planning Commission and City Council in its Bi-Annual Code Compliance reports.

This item is informational for the Council.

E.  PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT:
  TRAFFIC STUDY (PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH), GEORGE F CANYON NATURE
  CENTER REPLACEMENT PROJECT, STORMWATER PROJECTS UPDATE, PUBLIC
  WORKS PROJECTS UPDATE

  TRAFFIC STUDY (PVDN)

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), and
introduced Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineer with Willdan Engineering, who provided a
presentation summarizing traffic signal timing on PVDN and considerations of what can be done
to improve traffic delays.

Discussion ensued about various options for improvements and the effects each option has on
all directions of traffic, potential timing studies, as well as advanced signal technologies.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to re-
evaluate the signal timing at Palos Verdes Drive North and Rolling Hills Road, conduct a
timing study along the length of Palos Verdes Drive North at a future date once other
improvements have been completed, and explore advanced signal technologies.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
   GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT PROJECT

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

This item is informational for the Council.

  STORMWATER PROJECTS UPDATE – MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), and
summarized the Dry Well Project, the Torrance Airport Stormwater Basin Project, and the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Multi-Benefit Flow Diversion Feasibility Study.

This item is informational for the Council.

  PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS UPDATE (INCLUDING GRANTS)

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) on the Storm
Drain Repair Program, Rolling Hills Road Redevelopment Project, Street Re-surfacing &
Sidewalk Repair Projects, Dapplegray School and PVDN Intersection Improvements, Local
Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP) & Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grants,
Founders Park, Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC) Restrooms and Peartree Lane Utilities
and Sewer Line Work.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA inquired about a previous discussion related to Dapplegray
School and PVDN Intersection Improvements, in which the back access road could be
considered to create a loop for safer student drop-off and emergency vehicle access. It was
reported that staff contacted Dapplegray school and the School District, and staff has a meeting
with the PTA on April 9 related to this project. Staff noted this discussion will be coming back to
the City Council on April 23, and will include an update on the use of this back access road.

This item is informational for the Council.

7.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code Section 54957.6 Agency Designated
  Representatives: City Manager and Assistant City Manager Employee Organization: City
  of Rolling Hills Estates Employees' Association

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

8.  ADJOURNMENT

At 4:18 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the Regular City Council
meeting scheduled for Tuesday, April 9, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling
Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 26, 2024 (PDS)
